note: The raw fuzz input after the first selector byte is copied into a NUL-terminated IRC input buffer; the candidate begins with an IRCv3 message-tag prefix containing a tag value ending in a lone backslash.
With selector byte zero the harness forwards the copied line unchanged except for appending a newline, so the line still starts with '@' and keeps the trailing tag escape.
The IRC parser recognizes the leading '@' and records the message-tags substring for later parsing.
When no space follows the tag field, parsing does not reject or stop at the malformed lone tag escape; control returns with tags set and line at the string terminator.
Even though the command line is empty, the non-null tags pointer causes the tag-processing signal path to run.
The tag value string ending in a lone backslash is passed to the tag unescape routine.

On a backslash at the end of the tag value, tmp is advanced onto the string terminator and the surrounding for-loop then advances it again, so parsing continues beyond the intended end of the tag string.
